name: Synchrotron/VUV-laser ARPES energy-resolution test on polycrystalline gold at 7 K in UHV below 1E-10 mbar
plain_name: Measure electron energies knocked out of a cold surface by light
description: Cool a sample on a six-axis open-cycle liquid-helium-flow cryomanipulator to 7 K in a UHV analysis chamber kept below 1E-10 mbar, illuminate it with 21.2 eV photons (synchrotron or VUV laser) and fit the gold Fermi edge measured by a DA30 analyzer to obtain the combined energy resolution (2.67 meV); quantum materials are then measured, e.g. at 25 K.
keywords: Measure electron energies knocked out of a cold surface by light

sources.citation: Y.-C. Yang, Z.-T. Liu, J.-S. Liu, Z.-H. Liu, W.-L. Liu, X.-L. Lu, H.-P. Mei, A. Li, M. Ye, S. Qiao, D.-W. Shen, 'High-resolution ARPES endstation for in-situ electronic structure investigations at SSRF', arXiv:2102.09915

reported_equipment: six-axis open-cycle cryogenic manipulator (continuous-flow liquid helium cryostat)
BL03U beamline, Shanghai Synchrotron Radiation Facility

requirements.rationale: The gold Fermi-edge resolution test was performed at 7 K, the manipulator's lowest temperature.
Photoelectron spectroscopy is done under UHV to avoid surface contamination and electron scattering.
The analysis chamber is kept below 1E-10 mbar.
Synchrotron or VUV-laser photons must reach the cold sample and photoelectrons must reach the analyzer.
Optional: mu-metal shielding against the geomagnetic field protects low-energy photoelectron trajectories.
Optional: the reported quantum-material spectrum was taken at 25 K.
Optional: the reported manipulator is cooled by continuous liquid-helium flow.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
